relevance.rationale: Establishes a bijection between states on the part arc-graph of a link projection and states on the bichromatic arc-graph used in an earlier state-sum for the colored Jones polynomial, giving an elementary reproof of that state-sum formula, showing the two state models are not essentially distinct, and extending the formula from knots to links. Its closing section works out the crossing map sigma and the jump map tau explicitly for arbitrary 3-BRAID words, which is where it touches this corpus: every canonical QOU object is a 3-braid closure -- the Borromean nucleon is (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^3 and the figure-eight is (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^2 -- and the corpus computes their colored Jones via the Markov trace on H_3(q). This gives an INDEPENDENT state-sum route to the same invariant, which is precisely what the compute-author cross-check discipline asks for and which the corpus's Borromean colored-Jones producers do not currently have. It is supporting rather than core because nothing in the corpus is unsourced or incorrect for want of it: the value is verification, not correction. One consistency check already passes for free -- the document's component-count rule (word length in the Coxeter quotient congruent to 0 mod 6 gives three components) returns three for (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^3, matching the Borromean rings.

keyResults.locator: Sec. 9 (3-braid words), building on Thm 6.2 and Thm 7.1
keyResults.statement: For a 3-braid word the crossing permutation sigma and the jump map tau of the arc-graph state-sum are determined explicitly from the braid word by a finite case analysis, making the colored-Jones state-sum directly evaluable for any 3-braid closure.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent second method for the colored Jones of exactly the corpus's canonical braid class, usable as a cross-check on the Borromean colored-Jones producers rather than as a new input.

relevance.rationale: Genuine orphan. It establishes a bijection between states on the part arc-graph of a link projection (from the universal R-matrix of U_q(sl(2,C))) and states on the bichromatic digraph of the Garoufalidis-Loebl state sum, giving a new elementary proof of the knot state-sum formula, extending it from knots to links, and — the part that gives it a target here — discussing in detail the computation of the arc-graph state-sum for 3-BRAID CLOSURES. The folio's two canonical objects are exactly 3-braid closures: fundamental-knots-operator-basis records 4_1 = (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^2 and the Borromean rings L6a4 = (sigma_1 sigma_2^{-1})^3. So this supplies a genuinely independent combinatorial route to the same colored Jones data the folio obtains from the Hecke Markov trace, on precisely the braids the folio uses. That is a cross-check opportunity, not a result the folio consumes, hence supporting. Note the paper is a reconciliation result: its own conclusion is that the two state models are 'in fact not essentially distinct', so it should not be cited as offering a genuinely new invariant.

keyResults.statement: The R-matrix state sum on the part arc-graph and the Garoufalidis-Loebl bichromatic-digraph state sum are related by an explicit bijection of state sets, the formula extends from knots to links, and the arc-graph state-sum is computed explicitly for 3-braid closures.
keyResults.useForFolio: An independent state-sum route to the colored Jones polynomial of the folio's own canonical 3-braid closures, usable to cross-check the Markov-trace computation of tr_M on those words.

proposedActions.rationale: No ref() entry; supplies an independent computation route for the exact 3-braid closures the folio's operator basis is built from.
